title: What does Meroitic say?
place: Kingdom of Kush, middle Nile valley
summary: The Meroitic alphabet of ancient Kush was deciphered in 1909, so its texts can be sounded out, but the language itself remains poorly understood.
why: The written language of ancient Kush can be pronounced but barely understood.
question: What language is Meroitic, and what do its texts say?
evidence: Two script forms: cursive for records, hieroglyphic for royal and religious texts. The language died out around 400 CE; bilingual texts are scarce.
wouldSettle: More bilingual texts, or a secure link to a known language family.

theories.name: Nilo-Saharan (Eastern Sudanic)
theories.idea: Rilly argues from syntax, morphology and known vocabulary.

theories.name: Afroasiatic
theories.idea: Rowan argues from its sounds and Lipiński mainly from vocabulary.
